A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ScoreRS study. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable, and retained content can be matched across substantial reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original data-selection, reinforcement-learning, best-of-N, human-validation, and ablation results, including Skyscript and PPO experiments in its appendix.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains original experiments and adds human validation, scorer ablations, and filtering, reinforcement-learning, and best-of-N comparisons.

M1.justification: The stated preference-generation procedure changes: v2 replaces the earlier judging criteria with a unified five-dimension, 1–5 rubric and no longer specifies v1's confidence-above-3 selection rule. The Qwen2VL scoring architecture, pairwise loss, three-stage training, and reference-based reward remain intact. The PDFs do not establish whether existing preference pairs were regenerated.

E1.justification: The training sources and evaluated task coverage remain substantially identical: RS classification, retrieval, question answering, grounding, and LHRS-Bench understanding. New experiments reuse existing datasets with additional models, subsets, or annotation samples. VG-DOIR/VG-DIOR denotes the same grounding benchmark; multi-image change captioning is discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 adds SigLIP-2, labeled SigCLIP-2 in Table 12, and CLIP-LAION-RS filtering comparisons; DPO and GPT-4o reward comparisons; and LongCLIP-score and majority-voting best-of-N comparisons. Appendix B.4 also reports LHRS-Bot-Nova as a competing preference judge. These substantially expand comparator participation across ScoreRS applications.

E3.justification: The reported GRPO recipe changes from rank-128 LoRA to full-parameter training, 256 to 4096 generated tokens, KL coefficient 0.04 to 0.01, and revised batch size, learning rate, and duration (v1 Appendix 8.4; v2 D.5). Added designs include 3,000 distinct human-validation pairs, model-size/initialization controls, and 8K/26K DPO training. Retained Table 5 values do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds scorer-output normalization experiments, 2B-versus-7B and initialization ablations, 10%/20% retention sensitivity tests, expanded preference validation, and qualitative comparisons of ranked data (Appendices B.4, C, and E.1). These test reliability and design choices beyond v1's retained training-stage/data-component ablations and unsuccessful PPO experiment.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's model-human agreement reporting, v2 introduces inter-annotator agreement estimation using three annotators and 100 shared samples, split equally between caption and instruction preferences (B.4, Table 7). Neither version provides repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial human-validation, ablation, filtering, RL, and best-of-N results. Table 7 reports 90.06% caption and 96.80% instruction model-human agreement on new samples, separate from the retained 92.6% study. Most original scores, including Skyscript and PPO results, remain unchanged. Table 3 revises CLIP-P30S30/P30S60 HR-Pres. values from 65.97/66.94 to 65.90/66.90.

T1.justification: The Bradley-Terry formulation, pairwise negative-log-likelihood loss, reference-based reward equation, and deduplication similarity definitions are retained. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v2's introduction adds an explicit framework defining RS text quality to the first contribution. The central claims about ScoreRS, preference datasets, effective data filtering, reinforcement learning, and best-of-N selection remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of scorer size, initialization quality, extreme filtering, DPO data efficiency, and GPT-4o reward performance. It also acknowledges subjective caption judgments and explains when CLIP-score remains reasonable for short captions (B.4, C, F.1). These considerably expand the applicability qualifications and mechanism discussions.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents two nodes with eight A100-80G GPUs each, OLMo/LLaMA-Factory/VeRL frameworks, distributed reward-serving details, and explicit evaluation splits, grounding thresholds, and LHRS-Bench answer parsing. It also clarifies the equal-step RL control and expands scoring rubrics and prompts. Existing code, model, and dataset access links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially broadens the supporting literature to caption-quality evaluation, synthetic-data design, reward-model scaling, and DPO/RL data efficiency, including CLAIR, RS-RAG, DPO, and SigLIP-2. It also adds Falcon and ground–remote alignment to the RS discussion. The underlying positioning around RS-specific data curation remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites and condenses main-text explanations, moves related work before the method, relocates deduplication details to the appendix, and introduces the quality-dimension framing. The appendix is reorganized into sections A–F with a contents list and expanded thematic discussions.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 is redesigned around five quality dimensions, Figure 4 gains comparator curves, and new training, ablation, and ranking figures accompany validation, comparison, and rubric tables. Existing tables and examples are also resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important weaknesses in v1's empirical support: independent caption-and-instruction validation, alternative filtering/RL/selection methods, and scorer size/initialization ablations strengthen confidence in the central contribution. Detailed evaluation procedures and more qualified applicability discussions further improve assessability. Revised preference criteria and GRPO settings are not reconciled with largely retained headline results, leaving a reproducibility uncertainty, but the additional controls and validation provide a substantial net improvement.
